reviews.reasoning: Re-derived every claim from source. Quotes (כִּֽי אַתָּ֣ה אֱ֭לֹהִים שָׁמַ֣עְתָּ = 'For you, God, have heard my vows'; יָמִ֣ים עַל יְמֵי מֶ֣לֶךְ = 'You will prolong the king's life') match verse_map_web.json/verse_map_oshb.json exactly. The נדר ('vow') lexical bracket is accurate: oshb:Ps.61.6 has לִנְדָרָ֑י, oshb:Ps.61.9 has נְדָרַ֗י within לְֽשַׁלְּמִ֥י נְדָרַ֗י — a genuine internal inclusio that legitimately closes the strophe at the psalm's end, distinct from and complementary to the register shift (vow/heritage -> dynastic intercession -> vow of praise). boundary_evidence_refs are arithmetically correct (shift+1 psalm, verified against web_mt_offset_map.json). The device_notes' Elohistic-Psalter count ('no Yahweh and 3 Elohim occurrences') is exactly right per psalm_device_inventory.json yhwh_elohim_per_psalm['61'] = {'yhwh': 0, 'elohim': 3}; check_universals.py flags the phrase only because 'no Yahweh' lacks an explicit digit next to '3 Elohim', which is a style nit, not a factual defect — the underlying claim is true, so I am not filing it as a challenge. unit_type/confidence/parent grouping are all correctly formed.

The chosen span (ending exactly after the second occurrence of the byte/skeleton-close 'rock and salvation' line at MT 62:7) is structurally defensible as an envelope strophe closing before the register shift to public exhortation at 62:8 — collate.py confirms oshb:Ps.62.3's first three words are byte-identical to oshb:Ps.62.7's, and oshb:Ps.62.7's full text collates into oshb:Ps.62.3 at skeleton tier (62.3 carries one extra closing word, רַבָּֽה, that 62.7 lacks), matching the row's own claim there. But the row's stated WARRANT for the envelope is built on a misquoted translation, and several other claims in the row fail re-derivation. This is the most defect-dense row in the cluster; verdict is challenge on the accumulation of independently-verified, material defects below.

(the same 'wait in silence' idiom as web:Ps.62.1/oshb:Ps.62.2). The row instead glosses oshb:Ps.62.6 as "He alone is my rock and my salvation" — that English is verse_map_web.json['Ps.62.2']['clean'] / ['Ps.62.6']['clean'] (oshb:Ps.62.3/Ps.62.7's 'rock and fortress' idiom), a different recurring formula. The row's own next sentence then correctly collates oshb:Ps.62.2 vs oshb:Ps.62.6 as the (different-wording) silence idiom, silently abandoning the false 'rock and salvation' gloss it just gave for the same verse one clause earlier — the two idioms (silence at 62:2/62:6; rock-and-salvation at 62:3/62:7, which do collate near-verbatim) are conflated into a single 'same confidence idiom' claim.
